blocks.prompt: 8. If \(\sin\alpha = \dfrac{24}{25}\) and \(\cos\beta = \dfrac{20}{29}\), where \(0 < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and \(0 < \beta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}\). Show that \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{333}{725}\).
blocks.explanation:
Har angle ka ek ratio diya hai aur quadrant bhi (dono quadrant I mein).
\(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\) ke formula mein \(\cos\alpha\) aur \(\sin\beta\) bhi chahiye, jo diye nahi gaye.
Plan: \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\) se missing ratios nikalo (positive root), phir formula mein rakho.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\sin\alpha = \frac{24}{25}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{20}{29}\), dono angles quadrant I mein.
Saabit karna hai: \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{333}{725}\).
Tareeqa:
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
Is mein chaar values chahiye; do di hui hain, do hum nikalenge. Quadrant isliye diya gaya hai taake square root ka sign tay ho sake.

\(\cos\alpha\) nikalein
\[\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{576}{625}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{49}{625}}\]
\[= \dfrac{7}{25}\]
Kyun: \(\cos^2\alpha = 1 - \sin^2\alpha\), aur \(24^2 = 576\). Quadrant I mein saare ratios positive hote hain, is liye positive root liya.

\(\sin\beta\) nikalein
\[\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{400}{841}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{441}{841}}\]
\[= \dfrac{21}{29}\]
Kyun: \(\sin^2\beta = 1 - \cos^2\beta\); \(20^2 = 400\), \(29^2 = 841\), \(\sqrt{441} = 21\). Phir se quadrant I, to positive.

Formula mein rakhein
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \dfrac{24}{25}\cdot\dfrac{20}{29} - \dfrac{7}{25}\cdot\dfrac{21}{29}\]
\[= \dfrac{480}{725} - \dfrac{147}{725}\]
\[= \dfrac{333}{725}\]
Kyun: Dono products ka denominator \(25 \times 29 = 725\) hai, is liye seedha numerators minus kiye.
Dhyan dein: Sine of difference mein beech mein minus hi rehta hai; isay cosine wale formula se mat milayen.

Tasdeeq
\[24^2 + 7^2 = 625 = 25^2\]
\[20^2 + 21^2 = 841 = 29^2 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: (7, 24, 25) aur (20, 21, 29) Pythagorean triples hain, yani hamare nikale hue ratios bilkul durust hain.
